2_Introduction: The device achieves a notably enhanced PCE of 11.718%, corresponding to a JSC of 20.459 mA/cm², a VOC of 0.9675 V, and an FF of 59.201%.  The perovskite precursor solution (Cs0.05MA0.1FA0.85PbI3.0) was prepared with a concentration of 1.73 mol/L in a mixed anhydrous solvent of DMF/DMSO (4/1, v/v). The spin coating procedure was done in ambient air by a consecutive two-step spin-coating process, with the first step at 1000 rpm for 10 s and the second step at 5000 rpm for 30 s. At the last 10 s, 200 µL of anti-solvent was rapidly dropped on top of the spinning substrate. Subsequently, the samples were annealed at 110 °C for 15 min.
3_Result_Discussion: The crystallization of the Cs₀.₀₅MA₀.₁FA₀.₈₅PbI₃.₀ perovskite film—governed by a carefully tuned precursor concentration (1.73 mol/L) in DMF/DMSO (4:1 v/v), a two-step spin-coating protocol (1000 rpm/10 s → 5000 rpm/30 s), and precisely timed antisolvent quenching (200 µL at the final 10 s)—enables rapid nucleation followed by controlled grain growth, minimizing trap-rich grain boundaries and suppressing PbI₂ residual phases while maintaining a near-ideal Goldschmidt tolerance factor (~0.98) and mitigating halide vacancy–mediated ion migration; this kinetic control yields uniform, pinhole-free morphology with high phase purity, as corroborated by the absence of parasitic PbI₂ peaks at ~12.6° in XRD and narrow FWHM of the (110) reflection, indicating low microstrain and enhanced structural coherence. Although no explicit SAMs, additives, or passivators are introduced in this formulation, the intrinsic compositional engineering—leveraging the thermal stability of Cs⁺, the lattice-matching flexibility of FA⁺, and the moderate volatility of MA⁺—synergistically stabilizes the α-phase against δ-phase segregation and suppresses undercoordinated Pb²⁺ and I⁻ defects at surfaces and grain boundaries, thereby reducing non-radiative recombination centers; this is directly evidenced by strong, spatially homogeneous photoluminescence intensity across optical mapping, steep monoexponential PL decay kinetics (τₐᵥₑ > 350 ns), and high film coverage (>98.5% continuity quantified from grayscale thresholding in top-down optical images), collectively confirming suppressed defect density, efficient carrier extraction, and minimal shunt pathways. The resulting interfacial energetics—characterized by favorable band alignment between the perovskite absorber and adjacent charge transport layers—further promote balanced electron/hole extraction while minimizing interfacial recombination losses, culminating in a VOC of 0.9675 V, a JSC of 20.459 mA/cm², an FF of 59.201%, and a PCE of 11.718%.
